text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Tuesday.
- The negotiations on dual citizenship between Croatia and Yugoslavia to be postponed until the summer.
- A new agricultural policy may bring down the price of bread by some 20 percent, Agriculture Minister Zlatko Dominikovic said at a regular government press conference.
- Brewery Zagrebacka Pivovara, a subsidiary of Belgium's Interbrew, expects to produce more than 20,000 hectolitres of Stella Artois beer during 1997.
- Confectioner Kras plans to sell some 1,950 tonnes of its products in 1997, up 79 tonnes from 1996.
- Average net wage in January rose 2.6 percent to 2,274 kuna from last December, and 13.3 compared to January 1996.
- The Zagreb Auto Show and an agriculture exhibition open at the Zagreb trade centre.
- Prime Minister Zlatko Matesa met representatives of Texas-based corporations Enron and Enserch on Monday to discuss proposed energy projects in Croatia.
- Some 120,000 Croats are suffering from diabetes, with the figure on the rise as it is in the world.
- Employees of private food concern Agrokor sign a collective employment agreement with the management, envisaging a 15 percent salary increase.
- Some 208 tonnes of crude illegally shipped from Italy to Croatia thorugh a private smuggling channel.
- Dubrovnik's damaged Hotel Bellevue plans to raise five million kuna through a new share issue at 400 each.
- Splitska Banka deblocks pre-1991 citizens' currency savings up to a maximum of 3,000 German marks. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
